by a grenade that took away half her health. Although she later successfully countered and knocked down a Vietnamese player, she was ultimately defeated. Soopi became suspicious. She quickly checked the footage, realizing something was wrong, and started to investigate. >> Once the day's matches concluded, Soopi began reviewing the match recordings of. other players to compare them; she subsequently released a video as evidence, accusing two players of using "screen cheating" to track her location . Korean players specifically reviewed the live stream footage and discovered that the accused players did indeed turn their heads to check screens nearby. Moreover, those accused of " screen-peeking" were not ordinary streamers, but top-tier Vietnamese professional players, Hema and TanV, whom many fans familiar with the pro scene would recognize. The pair had previously delivered stellar. performances in several international tournaments, representing Vietnam in last year's PUBG All-Star event and clinching the championship, with Hema even earning the tournament MVP. Following the accusations from Ssubee, Hema and TanV issued an apology. However , they did not admit to direct screen-peeking, claiming instead that they had their stream chat open on a second monitor to interact with viewers during the match. They stated they only received external match information from viewers while checking the chat. The organizers also issued a statement, apologizing for the concerns regarding. competitive integrity, announcing that they would add delays to main broadcasts , enhance match monitoring, reissue operational guidelines, and remove the two players from subsequent stages. However, Korean players were dissatisfied with this announcement, criticizing it as too vague. It failed to name the specific region or the two players being sanctioned, leading to suspicions that the organizers were deliberately shielding them. Additionally, another Korean streamer stated that before the apology was released, Krafton had explicitly promised him that the Vietnamese side.

would issue an apology admitting to screen-peeking. When the official announcement finally dropped, it contained no admission of cheating, showing only the two Vietnamese players claiming they were just checking their chat. Outraged, this streamer led other Korean players in a collective boycott of the remaining tournament schedule. The authorities will continue to conduct a further investigation into the entire incident. By the way, the official Vietnamese PUBG account claimed that Ssubee was already showing signs of running out of power at the time. Not only that, they used the incident to make memes, directly posting photos of Ssubee and joking that he would be competing in the next tournament. On September 20th, officials announced that the event suffered from operational deficiencies and could no longer proceed , deciding to terminate the remaining schedule and distribute the $ 70,000 total prize pool equally among all. participating regions. During this period, many Korean players remained dissatisfied with how PUBG handled the situation. Consequently, tournament sponsors like the apparel brand NoGear and Billion Coffee were suddenly flooded with reports from numerous Korean players, forcing these brands to re-examine their sponsorship relationship with PUBG esports. This was especially true for NoGear, as their brand slogan is "Fair Play," representing their commitment to fair processes and legitimate competition. In addition, there were rumors circulating in the Vietnamese community at the time that Supi used three monitors, accusing him of screen-peeking to cheat. Some Vietnamese players also posted a screenshot, claiming that one could see his computer running other programs during his match stream, implying he might have been checking outside information. When Heima pinned this unverified claim during his stream, it.

caused many Vietnamese players to feel dissatisfied, believing the organizers were favoring the Korean players. Consequently, a large number of Vietnamese players flooded into Supi's channel, hurling insults and personal attacks in the comment section, and even editing photos of him in inappropriate ways. Not only that, but even the video that initially accused Heima and Mu was mass-reported and subsequently taken down. Facing the online harassment from Vietnamese players, Supi ultimately had no choice but to disable his comment section. He then stated in a video that being accused for no reason made him feel mentally exhausted, and even after. thinking for a long time, he still didn't understand what he had done wrong . At the same time, he expressed his disappointment in the organizers, believing that when he first raised the issue, Krafton should have stood by his side and provided him with the support he deserved. Furthermore, Supi clarified that his streaming setup only uses one monitor, and as of that time, there was no concrete evidence to prove that he was peeking. ...at screens. Until the afternoon of September 20th, Heima himself released a statement calling on his fans to stop attacking or harassing Supi and other players. He also acknowledged that his act of pinning comments on his channel had exacerbated. the entire incident, and promised to be more attentive to his live stream chat in the future. On September 23rd, the PUBG team finally released the investigation results and follow-up penalties regarding the controversy. The officials stated that after investigating through match broadcasts and the players 'personal perspectives, they confirmed that the two Vietnamese players did indeed stream-snipe during the match, violating PUBG's operational policies. Therefore, regardless of whether it was an exhibition match, the officials ensure the maintenance of fair competition. Ultimately, they decided to permanently ban the game accounts of " Blackma" and "Tanbu," and permanently disqualify both from participating in any PUBG tournaments organized or authorized by Krafton, including PGC, PGS, and PNC. As soon as the penalty results were announced, it immediately sparked an uproar in the community. Some players believe that whether it is direct stream-sniping or obtaining external match information by viewing live chat rooms, it is essentially cheating, so receiving a competitive ban is justified. However, other players expressed that while they support punishing stream-sniping players with competitive bans, they feel that a permanent game account ban combined with a lifetime competitive ban is too.

excessive, especially since it was only an exhibition match. Needless to say, the Vietnamese players were absolutely furious. The reason for this anger is that in October 2024, when Korean player "G-Ge" participated in the Korean PUBG League, viewers discovered a PUBG match spectator screen on his second monitor. He was questioned about whether he was stream-sniping at the time, but the officials ultimately did not impose any formal punishment on him, which is why this incident has now been brought up again by Vietnamese players. They brought it up again to criticize Krafton's approach as sheer double standards, arguing that the Korean player faced no punishment when. suspected of stream-sniping, yet the Vietnamese players were penalized so severely. Interestingly, a Vietnamese creator even produced a Korean song to mock Krafton's double standards, highlighting how one game can have different rules and different punishments. [This segment is a continuation of the previous one in the source.] Furthermore, Vietnamese players believe that PUBG esports has developed very well in Vietnam, with local league viewership peaks becoming some of the highest outside of world championships. Therefore, they feel that after contributing so much popularity to PUBG , they are being treated this way by Krafton, which makes them feel. disrespected. Consequently, on the day the officials announced the penalties, PUBG was hit with a massive wave of negative reviews on Steam. Furthermore, the team Tan belongs to issued a statement clarifying that while he did stream during the match, the event was merely an exhibition game. Since officials hadn't explicitly prohibited this behavior at the time, they argue that the players shouldn't bear full responsibility, let alone face such severe punishments as permanent bans and lifetime competitive disqualification. The team also stated that they are currently working with Krafton and relevant parties to verify the specific. rule citations and regulations used for this penalty. Given that Krafton has already admitted to lapses in tournament operation and incident handling, they believe that such career-ending permanent punishments should be subject to a fair, transparent, and consistent review process. Unexpectedly, in response to heavy criticism from Vietnamese players, Krafton chose to play hardball. Not only did they shut down the official Vietnamese PUBG accounts and indefinitely postpone the Vietnamese PUBG league, but they even removed the Vietnamese language resources from the game. These actions.

triggered a massive boycott among Vietnamese players, who urged others to uninstall the game, with local internet cafes even announcing that they had wiped PUBG from their systems. It is worth noting that FC Seoul had previously confirmed a collaboration with PUBG for an offline pop-up event. However, due to the backlash regarding PUBG’s handling of the tournament, FC Seoul canceled the partnership. Both HAS and Tan subsequently announced their formal departure from PUBG, even showing their uninstallation process to viewers during a live stream. In a follow-up. interview, the two stated that even if their lifetime competitive bans were lifted in the future, they would never return to this game. After leaving PUBG , the two have since switched to Delta Force. Ever since this incident erupted , Delta Force has surged to the top of the download charts on Google Play and the App Store in Vietnam. It seems the most straightforward business warfare is when your opponent sabotages themselves ; who would have thought that Tencent would be the ultimate beneficiary? All in all, this controversy has not only sparked intense dissatisfaction among Vietnamese players but has also led to conflicting views among players with different perspectives. On one hand, some believe that screen sniping or. obtaining external information via stream chats constitutes cheating, making the penalties reasonable. On the other hand, others feel that the permanent bans and lifetime competitive disqualifications handed down by Krafton are simply too excessive. Moreover, players are unhappy with the official's double standards, criticizing instances where Korean players previously engaged in screen sniping without facing formal repercussions, while Vietnamese players received such harsh punishments. This disparity is precisely what further fueled the Vietnamese player boycott of PUBG. What are your thoughts on the controversy surrounding PUBG Yaxin? 作者介紹了以直言不諱、常對遊戲產業發表看法而聞名的實況主 Asmongold。他受到不少玩家支持，卻也因不常洗澡、房間凌亂而被戲稱為「哥布林王」。如今，華裔加拿大實況主 Kacey 出現在他身邊，兩人的交往消息讓玩家驚訝不已，也讓她被稱作「精靈女王」。
